messages:
Sam: Quick follow-up from the precision profiles convo — we need to lock the service boundary: runtime-only opaque profiles vs API-first presets. Can we land on a pattern?
Aisha: Runtime-only keeps the API tiny but makes it harder for SEs/customers to opt per-request. I prefer API-exposed presets + server-controlled guardrails.
Marco: Agree with Aisha. We already have per-endpoint config; exposing presets (not raw bits) gives the customer signal without shifting safety to them.
Devon: If we expose presets, runtime must enforce quality floors and auto-fallbacks. Otherwise a bad profile deploy breaks customers.
Clare: Proposed minimal surface: presets + optional advisory hints. Example: ```json
{"precision":{"preset":"balanced", "hint_max_bits":8}}
```
Aisha: Also add a per-tenant flag `allow_freeform_precision` so enterprise accounts can lock to presets.
Marco: Storage note: store references to profile ids in route metadata, not full configs. Runtime should map profile_id -> quant artifact + safety metadata.
Devon: Runtime resolution table contents: model_family, profile_id, artifact_version, guard_flags, canary_state. Keep that private.
Sam: Telemetry: what fields are essential to detect quality regressions post-change?
Clare: Minimum: profile_id, sample_rate, model_version, cohort_id, metric_delta (e.g., avg_logprob_delta), and late_token_degradation_rate.
ops-bot: Ticket created: INF-3245 (telemetry schema) assigned to @Clare.
Aisha: Fallback behavior: if runtime detects quality floor breach for a profile, fallback to last-known-good profile, emit alert + rollback trace. No customer-visible error.
Marco: Canary flow: support `profile_id:canary/<id>` and percentage routing in the serving plane. Canary must be tied to observable thresholds.
Devon: API contract sketch: POST /v1/infer Body: {"model":"gptx-2", "prompt":"...", "precision":{"preset":"balanced", "max_bits":8, "min_bits":4, "quality_floor":0.96}}. Numeric hints advisory only.
Sam: Important: runtime should ignore numeric hints if tenant has profile lock. Hints are advisory by default.
Clare: Action items: 1) finalize preset taxonomy (high_quality, balanced, cost_saver, canary) 2) INF-3245 telemetry schema 3) runtime resolution table design 4) API doc PR for precision presets.
Sam: Timeline: prototype in next sprint, API doc in two sprints. OK?
Aisha: I can mock a resolution table and fallback harness for the prototype.
Marco: I'll draft the API PR and the preset taxonomy.
Devon: I'll write canary routing spec + threshold triggers for auto-fallback.
Clare: I'll own INF-3245 and telemetry work.
Sam: Risks: 1) numeric hints may be misinterpreted as SLA promises 2) keeping profile refs consistent across model upgrades 3) malformed profiles creating quality regressions -> exploited.
Aisha: Mitigations: sanitize and validate inputs server-side, require enterprise opt-in for freeform hints, rate limit profile creation, strong CI for profile artifacts.
Sam: Sounds good. I'll post a short RFC addendum with the decision: API presets + advisory numeric hints, runtime-owned resolution, auto-fallbacks, and telemetry. No objections by EOD means we start prototype. :thumbsup:
